newsitem.title: JAPAN: Charts point to respite for Japanese stocks.
newsitem.headline: Charts point to respite for Japanese stocks.

text.p: The pattern set by gyrating Japanese stocks over the last few sessions shows a technical support line for the Nikkei index above 17,000 points, which is likely to hold for a while, analysts said on Tuesday.
In the wake of Monday's strong rebound by the battered Nikkei benchmark, they said they could pinpoint a trough on technical charts that constitutes a support line for stocks.
Analysts said this was around 17,303 points, the Nikkei's closing low on Friday, or around 17,019, the intra-day low on Monday before the recovery, both of which are 17-month lows.
Analysts said stocks should fluctuate above 17,000 for a while and could retest the support line in February, as the market still lacks confidence in Japan's economic recovery.
They added that a break through the floor could trigger an accelerated drop towards 14,000.
Stocks have been in a downward spiral since December on worries about the economic impact of higher taxes and scepticism about the government's commitment to much-needed structural reforms.
But the Nikkei recovered more than 800 points on Monday in a correction from last week's accumulated loss of more than 2,000 points.
On Tuesday, the Nikkei ended virtually flat at 18,093.13, after plunging initially then popping briefly into positive territory as blue-chip buying boosted prices off their lows.

Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities, said that judging from Monday's rebound and the healthy turnover on the first two days of this week, the Nikkei average may have found a temporary floor.

Tetsuya Ishijima, chief strategist at Okasan Securities Co Ltd, said: "A sharp rebound after a nosedive forms a bottom on charts. Although the market environment is still unclear, the Nikkei could remain on a recovery trend for now."
"When the Nikkei nears 17,000 next time, buying demand will slow the fall," said a chartist at a major Japanese brokerage.
"But the Nikkei is still likely to head lower and form a triple bottom," he said.
Analysts said that if the Nikkei breached support at 17,000, there was no solid support line until close to 14,000.

This could set a third major bottom for the Nikkei since the start of Japan's economic recession in the early 1990s, following a 14,309 closing low for the Nikkei in 1992 and a 14,485 closing low in 1995.
Analysts said the market could come under selling pressure again in February, due to expected profit-taking before companies close their books at the end of March.
"There is likely to be more weakness in February before book-closing and especially if high-flying U.S. stocks start to falter," said Nikko's Ueki.
